NKJV.1: How the gold has become dim! How changed the fine gold! The stones of the sanctuary are scattered At the head of every street.
NKJV.2: The precious sons of Zion, Valuable as fine gold, How they are regarded as clay pots, The work of the hands of the potter!
NKJV.3: Even the jackals present their breasts To nurse their young; But the daughter of my people is cruel, Like ostriches in the wilderness.
NKJV.4: The tongue of the infant clings To the roof of its mouth for thirst; The young children ask for bread, But no one breaks it for them.
NKJV.5: Those who ate delicacies Are desolate in the streets; Those who were brought up in scarlet  Embrace ash heaps.
NKJV.6: The punishment of the iniquity of the daughter of my people Is greater than the punishment of the sin of Sodom, Which was overthrown in a moment, With no hand to help her!
NKJV.7: Her Nazirites were brighter than snow And whiter than milk; They were more ruddy in body than rubies, Like sapphire in their appearance.
NKJV.8: Now their appearance is blacker than soot; They go unrecognized in the streets; Their skin clings to their bones, It has become as dry as wood.
NKJV.9: Those slain by the sword are better off Than those who die of hunger; For these pine away, Stricken for lack of the fruits of the field.
NKJV.10: The hands of the compassionate women Have cooked their own children; They became food for them In the destruction of the daughter of my people.
NKJV.11: The LORD has fulfilled His fury,  He has poured out His fierce anger.  He kindled a fire in Zion, And it has devoured its foundations.
NKJV.12: The kings of the earth, And all inhabitants of the world, Would not have believed That the adversary and the enemy Could enter the gates of Jerusalem—
NKJV.13: Because of the sins of her prophets And the iniquities of her priests, Who shed in her midst The blood of the just.
NKJV.14: They wandered blind in the streets;  They have defiled themselves with blood,  So that no one would touch their garments.
NKJV.15: They cried out to them, “Go away, unclean! Go away, go away, Do not touch us!” When they fled and wandered, Those among the nations said, “They shall no longer dwell here.”
NKJV.16: The face of the LORD scattered them; He no longer regards them. The people do not respect the priests Nor show favor to the elders.
NKJV.17: Still our eyes failed us, Watching vainly for our help; In our watching we watched For a nation that could not save us.
NKJV.18: They tracked our steps So that we could not walk in our streets.  Our end was near; Our days were over, For our end had come.
NKJV.19: Our pursuers were swifter Than the eagles of the heavens. They pursued us on the mountains And lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
NKJV.20: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD,  Was caught in their pits, Of whom we said, “Under his shadow We shall live among the nations.”
NKJV.21: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, You who dwell in the land of Uz! The cup shall also pass over to you And you shall become drunk and make yourself naked.
NKJV.22: The punishment of your iniquity is accomplished, O daughter of Zion; He will no longer send you into captivity. He will punish your iniquity, O daughter of Edom; He will uncover your sins!

NASB.1: How dark the gold has become, [How] the pure gold has changed! The sacred stones are poured out At the corner of every street.
NASB.2: The precious sons of Zion, Weighed against fine gold, How they are regarded as earthen jars, The work of a potter's hands!
NASB.3: Even jackals offer the breast, They nurse their young; [But] the daughter of my people has become cruel Like ostriches in the wilderness.
NASB.4: The tongue of the infant cleaves To the roof of its mouth because of thirst; The little ones ask for bread, [But] no one breaks [it] for them.
NASB.5: Those who ate delicacies Are desolate in the streets; Those reared in purple Embrace ash pits.
NASB.6: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people Is greater than the sin of Sodom, Which was overthrown as in a moment, And no hands were turned toward her.
NASB.7: Her consecrated ones were purer than snow, They were whiter than milk; They were more ruddy [in] body than corals, Their polishing [was like] lapis lazuli.
NASB.8: Their appearance is blacker than soot, They are not recognized in the streets; Their skin is shriveled on their bones, It is withered, it has become like wood.
NASB.9: Better are those slain with the sword Than those slain with hunger; For they pine away, being stricken For lack of the fruits of the field.
NASB.10: The hands of compassionate women Boiled their own children; They became food for them Because of the destruction of the daughter of my people.
NASB.11: The LORD has accomplished His wrath, He has poured out His fierce anger; And He has kindled a fire in Zion Which has consumed its foundations.
NASB.12: The kings of the earth did not believe, Nor [did] any of the inhabitants of the world, That the adversary and the enemy Could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
NASB.13: Because of the sins of her prophets [And] the iniquities of her priests, Who have shed in her midst The blood of the righteous;
NASB.14: They wandered, blind, in the streets; They were defiled with blood So that no one could touch their garments.
NASB.15: 'Depart! Unclean!' they cried of themselves. 'Depart, depart, do not touch!' So they fled and wandered; [Men] among the nations said, 'They shall not continue to dwell [with us].'
NASB.16: The presence of the LORD has scattered them, He will not continue to regard them; They did not honor the priests, They did not favor the elders.
NASB.17: Yet our eyes failed, [Looking] for help was useless; In our watching we have watched For a nation that could not save.
NASB.18: They hunted our steps So that we could not walk in our streets; Our end drew near, Our days were finished For our end had come.
NASB.19: Our pursuers were swifter Than the eagles of the sky; They chased us on the mountains, They waited in ambush for us in the wilderness.
NASB.20: The breath of our nostrils, the LORD'S anointed, Was captured in their pits, Of whom we had said, 'Under his shadow We shall live among the nations.'
NASB.21: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, Who dwells in the land of Uz; [But] the cup will come around to you as well, You will become drunk and make yourself naked.
NASB.22: [The punishment] of your iniquity has been completed, O daughter of Zion; He will exile you no longer. [But] He will punish your iniquity, O daughter of Edom; He will expose your sins!

ESV.1: How the gold has grown dim, how the pure gold is changed! The holy stones lie scattered at the head of every street.
ESV.2: The precious sons of Zion, worth their weight in fine gold, how they are regarded as earthen pots, the work of a potter's hands!
ESV.3: Even jackals offer the breast; they nurse their young; but the daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.
ESV.4: The tongue of the nursing infant sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst; the children beg for food, but no one gives to them.
ESV.5: Those who once feasted on delicacies perish in the streets; those who were brought up in purple embrace ash heaps.
ESV.6: For the chastisement  of the daughter of my people has been greater than the punishment  of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, and no hands were wrung for her.
ESV.7: Her princes were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were more ruddy than coral, the beauty of their form  was like sapphire.
ESV.8: Now their face is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets; their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as wood.
ESV.9: Happier were the victims of the sword than the victims of hunger, who wasted away, pierced by lack of the fruits of the field.
ESV.10: The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food during the destruction of the daughter of my people.
ESV.11: The LORD gave full vent to his wrath; he poured out his hot anger, and he kindled a fire in Zion that consumed its foundations.
ESV.12: The kings of the earth did not believe, nor any of the inhabitants of the world, that foe or enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
ESV.13: This was for the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed in the midst of her the blood of the righteous.
ESV.14: They wandered, blind, through the streets; they were so defiled with blood that no one was able to touch their garments.
ESV.15: “Away! Unclean!” people cried at them. “Away! Away! Do not touch!” So they became fugitives and wanderers; people said among the nations, “They shall stay with us no longer.”
ESV.16: The LORD himself  has scattered them; he will regard them no more; no honor was shown to the priests, no favor to the elders.
ESV.17: Our eyes failed, ever watching vainly for help; in our watching we watched for a nation which could not save.
ESV.18: They dogged our steps so that we could not walk in our streets; our end drew near; our days were numbered, for our end had come.
ESV.19: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles in the heavens; they chased us on the mountains; they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
ESV.20: The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed, was captured in their pits, of whom we said, “Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.”
ESV.21: Rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom, you who dwell in the land of Uz; but to you also the cup shall pass; you shall become drunk and strip yourself bare.
ESV.22: The punishment of your iniquity, O daughter of Zion, is accomplished; he will keep you in exile no longer;  but your iniquity, O daughter of Edom, he will punish; he will uncover your sins.

NLT.1:
How the gold has lost its luster!
Even the finest gold has become dull.
The sacred gemstones
lie scattered in the streets!
NLT.2:
See how the precious children of Jerusalem,
worth their weight in fine gold,
are now treated like pots of clay
made by a common potter.
NLT.3:
Even the jackals feed their young,
but not my people Israel.
They ignore their children’s cries,
like ostriches in the desert.
NLT.4:
The parched tongues of their little ones
stick to the roofs of their mouths in thirst.
The children cry for bread,
but no one has any to give them.
NLT.5:
The people who once ate the richest foods
now beg in the streets for anything they can get.
Those who once wore the finest clothes
now search the garbage dumps for food.
NLT.6:
The guilt of my people
is greater than that of Sodom,
where utter disaster struck in a moment
and no hand offered help.
NLT.7:
Our princes once glowed with health —
brighter than snow, whiter than milk.
Their faces were as ruddy as rubies,
their appearance like fine jewels.
NLT.8:
But now their faces are blacker than soot.
No one recognizes them in the streets.
Their skin sticks to their bones;
it is as dry and hard as wood.
NLT.9:
Those killed by the sword are better off
than those who die of hunger.
Starving, they waste away
for lack of food from the fields.
NLT.10:
Tenderhearted women
have cooked their own children.
They have eaten them
to survive the siege.
NLT.11:
But now the anger of the LORD is satisfied.
His fierce anger has been poured out.
He started a fire in Jerusalem
that burned the city to its foundations.
NLT.12:
Not a king in all the earth —
no one in all the world —
would have believed that an enemy
could march through the gates of Jerusalem.
NLT.13:
Yet it happened because of the sins of her prophets
and the sins of her priests,
who defiled the city
by shedding innocent blood.
NLT.14:
They wandered blindly
through the streets,
so defiled by blood
that no one dared touch them.
NLT.15:
“Get away!” the people shouted at them.
“You’re defiled! Don’t touch us!”
So they fled to distant lands
and wandered among foreign nations,
but none would let them stay.
NLT.16:
The LORD himself has scattered them,
and he no longer helps them.
People show no respect for the priests
and no longer honor the leaders.
NLT.17:
We looked in vain for our allies
to come and save us,
but we were looking to nations
that could not help us.
NLT.18:
We couldn’t go into the streets
without danger to our lives.
Our end was near; our days were numbered.
We were doomed!
NLT.19:
Our enemies were swifter than eagles in flight.
If we fled to the mountains, they found us.
If we hid in the wilderness,
they were waiting for us there.
NLT.20:
Our king — the LORD’s anointed, the very life of our nation —
was caught in their snares.
We had thought that his shadow
would protect us against any nation on earth!
NLT.21:
Are you rejoicing in the land of Uz,
O people of Edom?
But you, too, must drink from the cup of the LORD’s anger.
You, too, will be stripped naked in your drunkenness.
NLT.22:
O beautiful Jerusalem, your punishment will end;
you will soon return from exile.
But Edom, your punishment is just beginning;
soon your many sins will be exposed.

AMP.15:
People cried to them, "Go away! Unclean!
Depart! Depart! Do not touch!"
So they fled, then they wandered [as fugitives];
People among the nations said,
"They shall not stay here any longer with us."
AMP.16:
The presence of the LORD scattered them [among the nations];
He will not continue to look after them.
They did not honor the priests;
They did not favor the elders.
AMP.17:
[And as for us,] yet our eyes failed,
Looking in vain for help.
Watching [from the towers] we watched
For a nation that could not save.
AMP.18:
The enemy hunted our steps,
So that we could not walk in our streets;
Our end drew near,
Our days were finished
For our end had come.
AMP.19:
Our pursuers were swifter
Than the eagles of the sky;
They pursued us on the mountains,
They waited in ambush for us in the wilderness.
AMP.20:
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD [our king],
Was captured in their snares,
He of whom we had said, "Under his shadow
We shall live among the nations."
AMP.21:
Rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom,
Who lives in the land of Uz.
But the cup [of the wine of God's wrath] will pass to you as well;
You will become drunk and make yourself naked.
AMP.22:
The punishment of your sin has been completed, O Daughter of Zion;
The LORD will no longer send you into exile.
But He will punish your sin, O Daughter of Edom;
He will expose your sins.

WEB.1: How the gold has become dim! The most pure gold has changed! The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.
WEB.2: The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, How are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!
WEB.3: Even the jackals draw out the breast, they nurse their young ones: But the daughter of my people has become cruel, like the ostriches in the wilderness.
WEB.4: The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst: The young children ask bread, and no man breaks it to them.
WEB.5: Those who fed delicately are desolate in the streets: Those who were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.
WEB.6: For the iniquity of the daughter of my people is greater than the sin of Sodom, That was overthrown as in a moment, and no hands were laid on her.
WEB.7: Her nobles were purer than snow, they were whiter than milk; They were more ruddy in body than rubies, their polishing was as of sapphire.
WEB.8: Their appearance is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: Their skin clings to their bones; it is withered, it has become like a stick.
WEB.9: Those who are killed with the sword are better than those who are killed with hunger; For these pine away, stricken through, for want of the fruits of the field.
WEB.10: The hands of the pitiful women have boiled their own children; They were their food in the destruction of the daughter of my people.
WEB.11: Yahweh has accomplished his wrath, he has poured out his fierce anger; He has kindled a fire in Zion, which has devoured its foundations.
WEB.12: The kings of the earth didn’t believe, neither did all the inhabitants of the world, That the adversary and the enemy would enter into the gates of Jerusalem.
WEB.13: It is because of the sins of her prophets, and the iniquities of her priests, That have shed the blood of the just in the middle of her.
WEB.14: They wander as blind men in the streets. They are polluted with blood, So that men can’t touch their garments.
WEB.15: “Go away!” they cried to them, “Unclean! Go away! Go away! Don’t touch! When they fled away and wandered, men said among the nations, “They can’t live here any more.”
WEB.16: Yahweh’s anger has scattered them; he will no more regard them: They didn’t respect the persons of the priests, they didn’t favor the elders.
WEB.17: Our eyes still fail, looking in vain for our help: In our watching we have watched for a nation that could not save.
WEB.18: They hunt our steps, so that we can’t go in our streets: Our end is near, our days are fulfilled; for our end has come.
WEB.19: Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky: They chased us on the mountains, they laid wait for us in the wilderness.
WEB.20: The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was taken in their pits; Of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall live among the nations.
WEB.21: Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Edom, that dwell in the land of Uz: The cup shall pass through to you also; you shall be drunken, and shall make yourself naked.
WEB.22: The punishment of your iniquity is accomplished, daughter of Zion; he will no more carry you away into captivity: He will visit your iniquity, daughter of Edom; he will uncover your sins.

MSG.1:
Oh, oh, oh...
How gold is treated like dirt,
the finest gold thrown out with the garbage,
Priceless jewels scattered all over,
jewels loose in the gutters.
MSG.2:
And the people of Zion, once prized,
far surpassing their weight in gold,
Are now treated like cheap pottery,
like everyday pots and bowls mass-produced by a potter.
MSG.3:
Even wild jackals nurture their babies,
give them their breasts to suckle.
But my people have turned cruel to their babies,
like an ostrich in the wilderness.
MSG.4:
Babies have nothing to drink.
Their tongues stick to the roofs of their mouths.
Little children ask for bread
but no one gives them so much as a crust.
MSG.5:
People used to the finest cuisine
forage for food in the streets.
People used to the latest in fashions
pick through the trash for something to wear.
MSG.6:
The evil guilt of my dear people
was worse than the sin of Sodom—
The city was destroyed in a flash,
and no one around to help.
MSG.7:
The splendid and sacred nobles
once glowed with health.
Their bodies were robust and ruddy,
their beards like carved stone.
MSG.8:
But now they are smeared with soot,
unrecognizable in the street,
Their bones sticking out,
their skin dried out like old leather.
MSG.9:
Better to have been killed in battle
than killed by starvation.
Better to have died of battle wounds
than to slowly starve to death.
MSG.10:
Nice and kindly women
boiled their own children for supper.
This was the only food in town
when my dear people were broken.
MSG.11:
God let all his anger loose, held nothing back.
He poured out his raging wrath.
He set a fire in Zion
that burned it to the ground.
MSG.12:
The kings of the earth couldn't believe it.
World rulers were in shock,
Watching old enemies march in big as you please,
right through Jerusalem's gates.
MSG.13:
Because of the sins of her prophets
and the evil of her priests,
Who exploited good and trusting people,
robbing them of their lives,
MSG.14:
These prophets and priests blindly grope their way through the streets,
grimy and stained from their dirty lives,
Wasted by their wasted lives,
shuffling from fatigue, dressed in rags.
MSG.15:
People yell at them, "Get out of here, dirty old men!
Get lost, don't touch us, don't infect us!"
They have to leave town. They wander off.
Nobody wants them to stay here.
Everyone knows, wherever they wander,
that they've been kicked out of their own hometown.
MSG.16:
God himself scattered them.
No longer does he look out for them.
He has nothing to do with the priests;
he cares nothing for the elders.
MSG.17:
We watched and watched,
wore our eyes out looking for help. And nothing.
We mounted our lookouts and looked
for the help that never showed up.
MSG.18:
They tracked us down, those hunters.
It wasn't safe to go out in the street.
Our end was near, our days numbered.
We were doomed.
MSG.19:
They came after us faster than eagles in flight,
pressed us hard in the mountains, ambushed us in the desert.
MSG.20:
Our king, our life's breath, the anointed of God,
was caught in their traps—
Our king under whose protection
we always said we'd live.
MSG.21:
Celebrate while you can, O Edom!
Live it up in Uz!
For it won't be long before you drink this cup, too.
You'll find out what it's like to drink God's wrath,
Get drunk on God's wrath
and wake up with nothing, stripped naked.
MSG.22:
And that's it for you, Zion. The punishment's complete.
You won't have to go through this exile again.
But Edom, your time is coming:
He'll punish your evil life, put all your sins on display.

NRSVCE.1:
How the gold has grown dim,
how the pure gold is changed!
The sacred stones lie scattered
at the head of every street.
NRSVCE.2:
The precious children of Zion,
worth their weight in fine gold —
how they are reckoned as earthen pots,
the work of a potter’s hands!
NRSVCE.3:
Even the jackals offer the breast
and nurse their young,
but my people has become cruel,
like the ostriches in the wilderness.
NRSVCE.4:
The tongue of the infant sticks
to the roof of its mouth for thirst;
the children beg for food,
but no one gives them anything.
NRSVCE.5:
Those who feasted on delicacies
perish in the streets;
those who were brought up in purple
cling to ash heaps.
NRSVCE.6:
For the chastisement of my people has been greater
than the punishment of Sodom,
which was overthrown in a moment,
though no hand was laid on it.
NRSVCE.7:
Her princes were purer than snow,
whiter than milk;
their bodies were more ruddy than coral,
their hair like sapphire.
NRSVCE.8:
Now their visage is blacker than soot;
they are not recognized in the streets.
Their skin has shriveled on their bones;
it has become as dry as wood.
NRSVCE.9:
Happier were those pierced by the sword
than those pierced by hunger,
whose life drains away, deprived
of the produce of the field.
NRSVCE.10:
The hands of compassionate women
have boiled their own children;
they became their food
in the destruction of my people.
NRSVCE.11:
The LORD gave full vent to his wrath;
he poured out his hot anger,
and kindled a fire in Zion
that consumed its foundations.
NRSVCE.12:
The kings of the earth did not believe,
nor did any of the inhabitants of the world,
that foe or enemy could enter
the gates of Jerusalem.
NRSVCE.13:
It was for the sins of her prophets
and the iniquities of her priests,
who shed the blood of the righteous
in the midst of her.
NRSVCE.14:
Blindly they wandered through the streets,
so defiled with blood
that no one was able
to touch their garments.
NRSVCE.15:
“Away! Unclean!” people shouted at them;
“Away! Away! Do not touch!”
So they became fugitives and wanderers;
it was said among the nations,
“They shall stay here no longer.”
NRSVCE.16:
The LORD himself has scattered them,
he will regard them no more;
no honor was shown to the priests,
no favor to the elders.
NRSVCE.17:
Our eyes failed, ever watching
vainly for help;
we were watching eagerly
for a nation that could not save.
NRSVCE.18:
They dogged our steps
so that we could not walk in our streets;
our end drew near; our days were numbered;
for our end had come.
NRSVCE.19:
Our pursuers were swifter
than the eagles in the heavens;
they chased us on the mountains,
they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
NRSVCE.20:
The LORD’s anointed, the breath of our life,
was taken in their pits —
the one of whom we said, “Under his shadow
we shall live among the nations.”
NRSVCE.21:
Rejoice and be glad, O daughter Edom,
you that live in the land of Uz;
but to you also the cup shall pass;
you shall become drunk and strip yourself bare.
NRSVCE.22:
The punishment of your iniquity, O daughter Zion, is accomplished,
he will keep you in exile no longer;
but your iniquity, O daughter Edom, he will punish,
he will uncover your sins.

NIV.1:
How the gold has lost its luster,
the fine gold become dull!
The sacred gems are scattered
at the head of every street.
NIV.2:
How the precious sons of Zion,
once worth their weight in gold,
are now considered as pots of clay,
the work of a potter’s hands!
NIV.3:
Even jackals offer their breasts
to nurse their young,
but my people have become heartless
like ostriches in the desert.
NIV.4:
Because of thirst the infant’s tongue
sticks to the roof of its mouth;
the children beg for bread,
but no one gives it to them.
NIV.5:
Those who once ate delicacies
are destitute in the streets.
Those nurtured in purple
now lie on ash heaps.
NIV.6:
The punishment of my people
is greater than that of Sodom,
which was overthrown in a moment
without a hand turned to help her.
NIV.7:
Their princes were brighter than snow
and whiter than milk,
their bodies more ruddy than rubies,
their appearance like sapphires.
NIV.8:
But now they are blacker than soot;
they are not recognized in the streets.
Their skin has shriveled on their bones;
it has become as dry as a stick.
NIV.9:
Those killed by the sword are better off
than those who die of famine;
racked with hunger, they waste away
for lack of food from the field.
NIV.10:
With their own hands compassionate women
have cooked their own children,
who became their food
when my people were destroyed.
NIV.11:
The Lord has given full vent to his wrath;
he has poured out his fierce anger.
He kindled a fire in Zion
that consumed her foundations.
NIV.12:
The kings of the earth did not believe,
nor did any of the world’s people,
that enemies and foes could enter
the gates of Jerusalem.
NIV.13:
But it happened because of the sins of her prophets
and the iniquities of her priests,
who shed within her
the blood of the righteous.
NIV.14:
Now they grope through the streets
like men who are blind.
They are so defiled with blood
that no one dares to touch their garments.
NIV.15:
“Go away! You are unclean!” men cry to them.
“Away! Away! Don’t touch us!”
When they flee and wander about,
people among the nations say,
“They can stay here no longer.”
NIV.16:
The Lord himself has scattered them;
he no longer watches over them.
The priests are shown no honor,
the elders no favor.
NIV.17:
Moreover, our eyes failed,
looking in vain for help;
from our towers we watched
for a nation that could not save us.
NIV.18:
Men stalked us at every step,
so we could not walk in our streets.
Our end was near, our days were numbered,
for our end had come.
NIV.19:
Our pursuers were swifter
than eagles in the sky;
they chased us over the mountains
and lay in wait for us in the desert.
NIV.20:
The Lord’s anointed, our very life breath,
was caught in their traps.
We thought that under his shadow
we would live among the nations.
NIV.21:
Rejoice and be glad, O Daughter of Edom,
you who live in the land of Uz.
But to you also the cup will be passed;
you will be drunk and stripped naked.
NIV.22:
O Daughter of Zion, your punishment will end;
he will not prolong your exile.
But, O Daughter of Edom, he will punish your sin
and expose your wickedness.

NET.1: א (Alef) Alas! Gold has lost its luster; pure gold loses value. Jewels are scattered on every street corner. ב (Bet)
NET.2: The precious sons of Zion were worth their weight in gold — Alas! — but now they are treated like broken clay pots, made by a potter. ג (Gimel)
NET.3: Even the jackals nurse their young at their breast, but my people are cruel, like ostriches in the desert. ד (Dalet)
NET.4: The infant’s tongue sticks to the roof of its mouth due to thirst; little children beg for bread, but no one gives them even a morsel. ה (He)
NET.5: Those who once feasted on delicacies are now starving to death in the streets. Those who grew up wearing expensive clothes are now dying amid garbage. ו (Vav)
NET.6: The punishment of my people exceeded that of of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment with no one to help her. ז (Zayin)
NET.7: Her consecrated ones were brighter than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies more ruddy than corals, their hair like lapis lazuli. ח (Khet)
NET.8: Now their appearance is darker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it is dried up, like tree bark. ט (Tet)
NET.9: Those who died by the sword are better off than those who die of hunger, those who waste away, struck down from lack of food. י (Yod)
NET.10: The hands of tenderhearted women cooked their own children, who became their food, when my people were destroyed. כ (Kaf)
NET.11: The LORD fully vented his wrath; he poured out his fierce anger. He started a fire in Zion; it consumed her foundations. ל (Lamed)
NET.12: Neither the kings of the earth nor the people of the lands ever thought that enemy or foe would enter the gates of Jerusalem. מ (Mem)
NET.13: But it happened due to the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who poured out in her midst the blood of the righteous. נ (Nun)
NET.14: They wander blindly through the streets, defiled by the blood they shed, while no one dares to touch their garments. ס (Samek)
NET.15: People cry to them, “Turn away! You are unclean! Turn away! Turn away! Don’t touch us!” So they have fled and wander about; but the nations say, “They may not stay here any longer.” פ (Pe)
NET.16: The LORD himself has scattered them; he no longer watches over them. They did not honor the priests; they did not show favor to the elders. ע (Ayin)
NET.17: Our eyes continually failed us as we looked in vain for help. From our watchtowers we watched for a nation that could not rescue us. צ (Tsade)
NET.18: Our enemies hunted us down at every step so that we could not walk about in our streets. Our end drew near, our days were numbered, for our end had come! ק (Qof)
NET.19: Those who pursued us were swifter than eagles in the sky. They chased us over the mountains; they ambushed us in the wilderness. ר (Resh)
NET.20: Our very life breath — the LORD’s anointed king — was caught in their traps, of whom we thought, “Under his protection we will survive among the nations.” ש (Sin/Shin)
NET.21: Rejoice and be glad for now, O people of Edom, who reside in the land of Uz. But the cup of judgment will pass to you also; you will get drunk and take off your clothes. ת (Tav)
NET.22: O people of Zion, your punishment will come to an end; he will not prolong your exile. But, O people of Edom, he will punish your sin and reveal your offenses!
